text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but the stock has been in a steep decline over the past two weeks, falling 9.6% from $154 to $136. The main driver appears to be uncertainty around geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—specifically fears about potential U.S. strikes on Iran and disruption to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Despite oil prices remaining elevated (U.S. crude at $99.64 per barrel, world crude at $107), the market seems worried that escalating Iran tensions could either trigger military action that disrupts supply or, conversely, de-escalate in a way that eases prices lower. The company also reported quarterly earnings on November 5th, but the timing of the selloff around the geopolitical headlines suggests that's the primary concern weighing on shares right now.

The wider context here is that oil and gas companies face a structurally uncertain oil price environment: crude is high enough to support strong cash flow, but geopolitical risk is creating volatility that makes investors hesitant to hold energy stocks. News that Trump said Iran strikes are "highly unlikely" if talks progress may have offered some relief today, but the underlying tension remains unresolved.
